summary: @qlik/eslint-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package declares itself an ESLint config for React but its scripts.preinstall (setup.mjs) downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into a temp directory, extracts and chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~730KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with a shuffled string array, opaque hex identifier renaming (WV8StW, hc1jfK9, etDiOOB,...) and a rotator function characteristic of obfuscator.io-style transforms. No source for this bundle is shipped and no ESLint configuration logic requires an alternate-runtime install. Executing the payload under a freshly-downloaded runtime is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based scanners. The @qlik scope resembles Qlik's open-source namespace while the shipped install behavior is unrelated to ESLint configuration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
